params.baseInstructions: Complete the supplied mathematical task using only its explicit inputs and tools. Submit the requested JSON artifact through structured submit_draft (preferred) or the compatible submit_artifact wrapper. Tool feedback is real task feedback; do not invent a successful check. When a submit tool returns stage_complete:true, end your turn immediately. This controller handles subsequent stages; do not keep calling tools or seek a later-stage verdict here. This is a Yui workflow stage. Read the relevant declared Yui rules, preserve the supplied proof route and exact allowed assumptions, and distinguish mathematical review from structural checks.

dynamicTools.name: read_task_input
dynamicTools.description: Read an explicitly frozen task document by ID; no other local files are accessible.

dynamicTools.name: read_yui
dynamicTools.description: Read declared Yui rules/templates; no tests, historical runs or personal files.

dynamicTools.name: check_artifact
dynamicTools.description: Check a JSON artifact against the explicit stage contract; this is not automatic mathematical certification.

dynamicTools.name: submit_artifact
dynamicTools.description: Submit a JSON artifact after its stage checks.

dynamicTools.name: report_obstacle
dynamicTools.description: Report exact status, location, explanation, basis, partial_progress. SUBSTANTIVE_GAP or SUSPECTED_GAP stops for an actual unsupported mathematical implication; give its premises, conclusion and mathematical grounds. SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE or INPUT_CONFLICT stops for a real source-access/original-input obstacle. Ordinary unfinished drafting, source registration or format work must use TASK_INCOMPLETE: this records progress without ending the stage; continue the actual work. Difficulty or artifact incompletion alone is not a mathematical gap.

dynamicTools.name: check_draft
dynamicTools.description: Preferred structured-object form of check_artifact: provide artifact as an actual JSON object, not an escaped JSON string. Same complete validation and acceptance scope.

dynamicTools.name: submit_draft
dynamicTools.description: Preferred structured-object form of submit_artifact: provide artifact as an actual JSON object, not an escaped JSON string. Same complete validation and acceptance scope.

input.text:
Perform an actual fresh packet-only Audit A replay. Read packet.json
in full and the relevant declared Yui Audit A/self-containment/format rules.
This packet is your only mathematical task material. Treat its inputs as the
allowed conditional premises; source fidelity is checked separately. Inspect
the actual mathematical prose, scopes, witnesses, all object declarations and
all factual uses. Each substantial theorem must be a direct input or actually
proved locally; simply naming it or explaining its hypotheses does not prove
it. Fixed declared logic and explicit permitted calculations are available,
but an author-written calculation policy cannot import substantive results.
Return JSON {inference,packet_sha256,verdict,notes,checks,findings}. checks has
exactly inputs,argument,dependency_accounting,output,scope,applicability,
statement_closure,object_closure,dependency_closure,packet_replay. Each is
{verdict:PASS|FAIL|UNVERIFIED,notes,locations:[resolving JSON pointers into this
packet]}. Give actual specific judgments. Locate the first unsupported
implication if present; do not repair the supplied argument or substitute a
different proof. For packet_replay judge sufficiency from this packet alone.
Carrier identity, canonical hash binding and transmitted-material readback
are checked outside your mathematical review. State your real input boundary,
without inventing runtime attestation or asking for extra source proofs.
The packet_replay verdict is the mathematical conditional: given the externally
checked carrier/input boundary, does this packet alone suffice? You do not
certify execution isolation. Missing access to runtime logs is therefore not a
mathematical UNVERIFIED finding for packet_replay. Preserve actual mathematical
uncertainty or insufficiency, and state your own read boundary honestly. The
controller separately rejects unqualified execution before accepting the review.

Yui entry: read_yui(path="SKILL.md", start=1, end=200). Available frozen rule paths (relative to rigorous-proof): SKILL.md, references/audit-a.md, references/external-theorems.md, references/isolation.md, references/lean-handoff.md, references/logical-rules.md, references/measurement.md, references/nl0-authoring.md, references/nl0-format.md, references/nl0-stage.md, references/self-containment.md, templates/audit-a.md, templates/authoring.md, templates/submission-example.md, translation/references/architecture.md, translation/references/audit-b.md, translation/references/design-notes.md, translation/references/experiments.md, translation/references/integrated-workflow.md, translation/references/obstacle-routing.md, translation/references/shared-lemmas.md, translation/references/source-refactoring.md, translation/references/stage.md, translation/references/translation-rules.md, translation/references/workflow.md, translation/templates/audit-b.md, translation/templates/source-refactoring.md. Every read supports at most 250 lines. Start with the entry and follow its relevant links; do not guess filenames.
Frozen task document IDs: packet.json. Use read_task_input to read them.
Prefer check_draft/submit_draft with an actual artifact JSON object. The older check_artifact/submit_artifact wrappers require artifact_json to be a double-encoded valid JSON string; do not supply Python dictionaries or single-quoted keys. Both forms run identical checks.
